summary: Deployed a 3-node RabbitMQ cluster (node1/node2/node3, CentOS Stream 10, RabbitMQ 3.13.7 / Erlang 26.2.5.4) serving AMQP exclusively over TLS on port 5671, using a dedicated CA generated on node1. mTLS is enforced (verify_peer, fail_if_no_peer_cert=true) so only clients presenting a certificate issued by that CA can connect; plaintext AMQP (5672) is disabled entirely. The management HTTP API (15672) is reachable only from the cluster's own /24 subnet via a dedicated firewalld zone scoped to that subnet; the node-facing public zone exposes only 5671/tcp. All three nodes were then restarted one at a time with quorum preserved, boot_id changes proved real reboots, and RabbitMQ/cluster/TLS/management-restriction health was re-verified after each.
actions_performed: Installed erlang + rabbitmq-server on all 3 nodes via packagecloud.io rabbitmq/erlang and rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server el/9 repos (only working repo path for CentOS Stream 10)
Populated /etc/hosts with CLUSTER_HOSTS and set up inter-node SSH from node1 for cert/cookie distribution
Generated a dedicated CA (RabbitMQ Cluster CA, 4096-bit RSA, 10y validity) on node1
Generated per-node server certs (CN=nodeN, SAN=DNS:nodeN + node's cluster IP) signed by that CA and distributed to /etc/rabbitmq/tls on each node
Generated a CA-signed test client cert and a self-signed untrusted client cert for negative testing
Generated and distributed a shared Erlang cookie to /var/lib/rabbitmq/.erlang.cookie (mode 400) on all nodes
Wrote rabbitmq.conf on all nodes: listeners.tcp=none, listeners.ssl.default=5671 with cacertfile/certfile/keyfile, ssl_options.verify=verify_peer, fail_if_no_peer_cert=true, management.tcp.port=15672
Enabled rabbitmq_management plugin and started rabbitmq-server on all nodes
Created firewalld zone 'rabbitcluster' scoped to source 10.100.114.0/24 on each node opening 4369/25672/5671/15672 only to cluster peers; public zone only opens 5671/tcp
Joined node2 and node3 to node1's cluster via rabbitmqctl join_cluster; confirmed 3/3 running nodes
Created cluster_admin administrator user with a generated password, deleted default guest user

Verified via openssl s_client: CA-signed client cert handshake succeeds (Verification: OK); untrusted self-signed cert rejected with 'bad certificate' alert; no client cert rejected with 'handshake failure' alert
Verified full AMQPS publish/consume with pika using the CA-signed client cert against all three node IPs
Verified management API returns 401 without valid RabbitMQ credentials and 200-class success with cluster_admin credentials from a cluster peer, while public-zone firewall config exposes only 5671
Captured pre-restart boot_id and cluster/service health baseline on all 3 nodes

Sequentially rebooted node1, then node2, then node3 via systemctl reboot, polling until reachable, confirming changed boot_id after each, waiting for rabbitmq-server active and full 3/3 cluster quorum before proceeding to the next node
Post-restart re-verified AMQPS+mTLS functional test, untrusted-cert rejection, and management-port firewall restriction on all nodes

evidence.summary: join_cluster on node2 and node3, then cluster_status on node1 shows 3 disk nodes / 3 running nodes

evidence.requirement: AMQP served only over TLS (plaintext disabled)
evidence.summary: rabbitmqctl status listeners show amqp/ssl on 5671 only, no plain 5672 listener; ss -tlnp confirms no 5672 socket

evidence.requirement: Certificate authority created for this cluster and used to issue node/client certs
evidence.summary: Self-signed CA generated (CN=RabbitMQ Cluster CA); per-node server certs and a client cert signed by that CA with correct SANs/subjects

evidence.requirement: Only clients presenting a certificate issued by the cluster CA are accepted (mTLS enforced)
evidence.summary: openssl s_client: CA-signed client cert handshake succeeds with Verification: OK; self-signed untrusted cert rejected with bad-certificate TLS alert; no-cert connection rejected with handshake-failure alert

evidence.requirement: AMQPS functions end-to-end with CA-issued client cert across all cluster nodes
evidence.summary: pika client using the trusted client cert publishes and consumes a message against node1, node2, and node3 over port 5671

evidence.requirement: Management interface reachable only from within the cluster
evidence.summary: firewalld 'rabbitcluster' zone (source 10.100.114.0/24 only) opens 15672 on all nodes; the node-facing public/default zone lists only 5671/tcp (no 15672); a cluster-peer request to the management API returns 401 (reaches the app) while auth correctly rejects bad credentials and accepts valid ones
